key_insight: A three-dimensional model predicts strong angular variation in energy dissipation where equal liquid jets collide, even with uniform inlet and sheet mean velocities.
engineering_relevance: Angularly resolved dissipation estimates could inform the design of impinging-jet mixers where local mixing intensity matters.
method: Model collision-region thickness as varying linearly from the stagnation point to the outer boundary along each radial line.
Combine modeled volume with collision-induced kinetic energy loss to calculate overall dissipation per unit mass.
Calculate local dissipation averaged over narrow angular sectors.
evidence_signal: The model recovers the cylindrical-region limit for directly opposed jets, and preliminary micromixing results are consistent with its predicted angular variation.
watch_item: The assumed collision-region geometry and the location of energy dissipation still require independent validation.
paper_title: Azimuthally Resolved Energy Dissipation Rates in the Impingement Zone of Equal Free Impinging Liquid Jets: A Three-Dimensional Model
